Symptom: After opening a context menu (app icon or stolen tray indicator), moving the mouse pointer across adjacent icons immediately closes the current menu and opens the menu of the hovered icon without clicking; Moving the mouse cursor to click a lower menu item in a tray menu triggers the main panel context menu instead
Trigger: Open a context menu on an app icon or stolen tray indicator, then move the mouse cursor across adjacent icons or panel space

target_diagnosis.expected_behavior: Context menus open strictly on an explicit right-click action and never switch automatically upon hovering over adjacent icons or panel areas
target_diagnosis.root_cause: Main.panel.menuManager (an instance of PopupMenuManager) implements active menu hover-cycling designed for top panel menu bars (File -> Edit -> View). Registering custom extension PopupMenus or stolen statusArea indicators in Main.panel.menuManager activates hover-switching across all registered actors. Additionally, attaching right-click listeners to the root container (_dockContainer) receives event bubbling from all child branches in Clutter.

failed_approaches.approach: Returning Clutter.EVENT_STOP on root container button-press-event for tray icons
failed_approaches.result: Cancels Clutter pointer grab and suppresses button-release-event and clicked signals on target children, making tray icons unresponsive
Intercepts and blocks normal left-clicks on tray icons whenever an indicator menu is open

target_diagnosis.fix_summary: Call Main.panel.menuManager.removeMenu(indicator.menu) on stolen indicators and avoid registering extension menus with Main.panel.menuManager. Move right-click background listeners from root container to _appsScrollView, mark interactive actors with _blocksDockContextMenu = true, and debounce single-turn menu closes via GLib.idle_add.

manual_steps: Right click an app icon or stolen tray indicator to open its context menu
Move the mouse pointer over adjacent tray icons and app icons without pressing any button
Verify that no adjacent context menu opens on hover
Click menu items or click outside to verify clean dismissal

regression_risks: Stolen tray indicator menus not closing when clicking outside
Interference between app icon context menus and panel background context menu

Stack: gnome-shell, gjs, clutter, st
Versions: OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (Linux x86_64), Runtime: GNOME Shell 42.9 (GJS 1.72.4)
Symptom: St.ScrollView inside a vertical St.BoxLayout collapses to 1px height when child grid layout returns naturalHeight = 4294967296; App launcher or icon grid is created but invisible on screen despite appsScroll=1, appsBox=1, status=4294967040 in debug logs; get_preferred_height() returns naturalHeight = 4294967296 (uint32 sentinel for -1) breaking container height allocation math
Trigger: Add a custom grid layout container inside a St.ScrollView within a vertical St.BoxLayout, where a child actor has conflicting alignment, missing min-size, or calls queue_relayout during construction

target_diagnosis.expected_behavior: St.ScrollView expands smoothly within the vertical St.BoxLayout according to available container space, displaying icon grids correctly without collapsing to 1px
target_diagnosis.root_cause: Child layout actor returns an unconstrained preferred height sentinel (-1), which when stored or converted to unsigned 32-bit integer (uint32) in Clutter/St C layout math becomes 4294967296 (2^32). When vertical St.BoxLayout calculates natural height allocations across siblings, this overflowed value forces St.ScrollView to allocate 1px minimum height instead of remaining available vertical space.

failed_approaches.approach: Setting arbitrary min-height in CSS without resolving alignment conflicts
failed_approaches.result: ScrollView stays fixed size or clips content without responding dynamically to panel size changes

failed_approaches.approach: Calling actor.queue_relayout() inside container build constructor
failed_approaches.result: Triggers recursive layout recalculation during GObject init causing state inconsistency and empty AppFavorites race condition

failed_approaches.approach: Relying on multiple parent actors to manage child geometry simultaneously
failed_approaches.result: Creates geometry owner conflict where competing actors continuously override allocation boxes

target_diagnosis.fix_summary: Remove conflicting x_align/y_align parameters on container actors, set explicit min-width and min-height constraints on custom actors, avoid calling queue_relayout during construct, safely reset preferred size using set_height(-1), and establish a single geometry owner per layout hierarchy.

manual_steps: Install and enable minimal reproduction extension in GNOME Shell
Open side panel or dock containing St.ScrollView
Verify that appsScroll allocation height is greater than 100px and icons render properly
Verify naturalHeight is positive and <= available monitor height

regression_risks: ScrollView overflowing panel boundary when total item count is small
Transient empty AppFavorites grid on initial GNOME Shell startup if AppSystem is not ready
Accessing disposed DockAppIcon references during async icon rebuild

target_diagnosis.expected_behavior: Stolen tray indicators preserve active state and render cleanly in 32x32px slots inside a 3-column row grid
target_diagnosis.root_cause: Indicators inherit top-panel theme rules (-natural-hpadding, -minimum-hpadding) and container alignment parameters from Main.panel._rightBox. Adding them directly to custom containers without state saving, CSS resets, and size constraining distorts layout.

Verify indicator icons align in 32x32px slots in a 3-column grid
Disable extension and verify indicators return to default top panel undamaged

Trigger: Add a custom panel to GNOME Shell and maximize any application window

target_diagnosis.expected_behavior: Mutter reserves screen edge space according to dock width and automatically constrains maximized/tiled application windows outside the dock area
target_diagnosis.root_cause: Adding a custom panel actor using Main.layoutManager.addChrome() without specifying affectsStruts: true. Mutter's layout manager remains unaware that screen edge space must be reserved and does not emit _NET_WM_STRUT_PARTIAL window constraints.

failed_approaches.result: Overridden by Mutter window manager during workspace restacking and window creation

target_diagnosis.fix_summary: Pass affectsStruts: true in Main.layoutManager.addChrome(dockActor, { affectsStruts: true, affectsInputRegion: true, trackFullscreen: true }). Mutter automatically creates and manages window struts for the panel actor.
